TL;DR: Mid-market SaaS (customer engagement) evaluating Redwood Hosted first with plan to move to Dedicated if POC meets latency and quality gates. Primary workload = multi-turn chat agents with tool-calling (calendar, docs search, create-ticket) + structured outputs for downstream actions. Latency SLOs: 95th percentile streaming latency target 150ms for agent token delivery (customer measures perceived response time). Current POC status: Hosted API POC (6w) ingesting 3 canonical prompts and ~25k historical sessions for eval. Early numbers: 95p ~180ms, tail spikes during bursts; SE suggested prefix caching and smaller quantized fallback for cost control.

Quality/gating: Customer requires prompt/eval regression gating — cannot accept regressions in agent behavior when optimizing for latency. They want an automated pipeline: baseline eval set -> A/B canary rollouts -> automatic rejection if quality delta exceeds threshold. Proposed rollout: 5-10% canary, monitor per-route intent accuracy and hallucination rate + human review set, then ramp (25% -> 50%). Customer: "We can’t trade away correctness for a few ms. If agent starts missing actions, product team rejects the rollout." — CTO (paraphrase).

Operational needs: streaming with low-token latency, tool-calling reliability (idempotency, retries), observability per-route (token cost + latency + error), audit logs for actions, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys, US data residency preferred. Cost sensitivity: tight on per-token spend; interested in recommendations (batching thresholds, quantization levels, model routing) — Redwood Optimize value prop resonates.

Next steps / asks: SE to deliver dedicated pricing ladders (steady throughput + burst) and example canary roll playbook; Dev team to provide SOC2 artifact list; finalize eval metrics and thresholds; run a controlled canary (hosted) using Redwood canary tooling and eval gating.
